polls.note: [Genial/Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) national poll published Aug 5 (G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, Valor Econômico, O Globo, Estadão, VEJA, JOTA, Money Times, Poder360, Brasil de Fato). [First round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) Lula 39% x Flávio 30% (gap +9pp), with Caiado 4%, Renan Santos 4%, Zema 2%, Augusto Cury 1%, Cabo Daciolo 1%, Samara Martins 1%, blank and void 8%, undecided 10%. [Runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) Lula 44% x Flávio 39% (gap +5pp, blank and void 13%, undecided 4%); Lula 46% x Zema 34%; Lula 45% x Caiado 37%; Lula 45% x Renan Santos 35%. Lula wins all four runoff scenarios. REJECTION: 54% would not vote for Flávio and 41% would; 52% would not vote for Lula and 45% would. WITHIN-HOUSE COMPARISON, which is the only valid one: in the Jul 15 round it was 40% x 28%, a +12pp gap, and in the runoff 45% x 37%, a +8pp gap. So the first-round gap fell 3pp and the runoff gap fell 3pp, and the movement belongs to the challenger, who gains 2pp in the first round and 2pp in the runoff while Lula gives up 1pp in each. GOVERNMENT APPROVAL: 48% approve and 47% disapprove, with 5% no answer, numbers IDENTICAL to its own Jul 15 round. Administration ratings also repeat exactly: 36% positive, 26% average, 36% negative, 2% no answer. Two rounds by the same house with the same number on both indicators describe immobility, not a trend. Fieldwork Jul 31 to Aug 3, n=2,004, in person, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, commissioned by Banco Genial, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) registration BR-06591/2026.
polls.source: Genial/Quaest via G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, Valor Econômico, O Globo, Estadão, JOTA, Money Times Aug 5

polls.note: Meio/Ideia (Instituto Ideia with Canal Meio) national poll published Aug 5 (Exame, Gazeta do Povo, JOTA, Estadão, Valor Econômico, Folha de S.Paulo, CartaCapital, Congresso em Foco). [First round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) Lula 43% x Flávio 35% (gap +8pp), with Caiado 5.7%, Renan Santos 4.7%, Zema 2.6%, Augusto Cury 1.7%, Cabo Daciolo 0.6%, Samara Martins 0.3%, Edmilson Costa 0.2%, Hertz Dias and Rui Costa Pimenta 0.1% each, blank and void 2%, don't know 4%. UNPROMPTED VOTE, which is a different question and does not mix with the prompted one: Lula 34.4%, Flávio 23%, undecided 27.7%. [Runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) Lula 48.5% x Flávio 43% (gap +5.5pp); Lula 48.5% x Zema 37%; Lula 48.5% x Caiado 40%; Lula 48% x Renan Santos 34.7%. Lula wins all four. WITHIN-HOUSE COMPARISON: in the Jul 8 round it was 40.4% x 32%, a +8.4pp gap, and in the runoff 45% x 40%, a +5pp gap. The first-round gap barely moved, from +8.4pp to +8pp, and neither did the runoff, from +5pp to +5.5pp. What rose were BOTH: Lula from 40.4% to 43% and Flávio from 32% to 35%, which describes vote concentrating on the top two rather than an advantage for either. Fieldwork Jul 31 to Aug 3, n=1,500, telephone, 2.5pp margin, 95% confidence, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) registration BR-04579/2026.
polls.source: Meio/Ideia via Exame, Gazeta do Povo, JOTA, Estadão, Valor Econômico, Folha de S.Paulo Aug 5

polls.note: [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) national poll released Aug 3, the 8th round in the series, and the first of the four national polls the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) filing had scheduled between Aug 3 and Aug 5. First round Lula 41% x Flávio 37%, with Caiado at 5%, Renan Santos at 4% and Zema at 3%. Runoff Lula 46% x Flávio 45%, a 1pp difference that falls WITHIN the 2pp margin and is therefore a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico). Fieldwork Jul 31 to Aug 2, n=2,002, telephone, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, filing BR-02874/2026. WHAT CHANGES THE WEEK IS THE COMPARISON WITH THE INSTITUTE'S OWN PREVIOUS ROUND: the first-round gap FELL FROM 9pp TO 4pp in a single round, against the 42% x 33% of Jul 27. And the move comes almost entirely from one side, because LULA GAVE UP 1pp and FLÁVIO GAINED 4pp. In the runoff the tightening is sharper still, from 4pp to 1pp, with Lula going from 47% to 46% and Flávio from 43% to 45%. The round's other runoffs: Lula 46% x Caiado 42%, Lula 46% x Zema 40% and Lula 47% x Renan Santos 37%. AGAINST THE OTHER HOUSES, among the four national polls released since Jul 29 this is the one showing the tightest first round: 4pp here, against 6pp in PoderData of Jul 30, 9.1pp in [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29 and 9.3pp in Vox Brasil of Jul 31. The distance between the highest and the lowest reading reaches 5.3pp and is larger than any price move in the period. ⚠️ REJECTION NOT PUBLISHED BY THIS PANEL: the secondary sources DISAGREE. Poder360, CNN Brasil and Correio Braziliense report 49% for each of the two; Money Times reports 50% for Lula and 51% for Flávio. The institute's release note does not carry the figure, so it could not be settled against a primary source and the number stays out, with the disagreement declared here. ⚠️ CORRECTION PUBLISHED ON Aug 4: this entry said the round had carried no approval figures, and it had. The data came out in the Aug 4 coverage, from the SAME round BR-02874/2026: government approval at 47% against 48% disapproval, and administration ratings at 37% excellent or good, 18% average and 43% poor or terrible. The panel corrects rather than rewriting in silence.
polls.source: BTG/Nexus via the institute's own site (nexus.fsb.com.br), Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão, CNN Brasil, JOTA, CartaCapital, Poder360, VEJA, Exame, Correio Braziliense and Money Times Aug 3. TSE filing BR-02874/2026.

polls.note: Vox Brasil national poll published Jul 31 (Metrópoles, Revista Fórum, Contracs). First round Lula 40.5% x Flávio 31.2% (gap +9.3pp), with Caiado 5.5%, Zema 3.2% and Renan Santos 3.0%. Runoff Lula 47.5% x Flávio 41.1% (gap +6.4pp), a difference that falls OUTSIDE the two margins added together and therefore is NOT a statistical tie, unlike PoderData of Jul 30, which gave 3pp. Field Jul 26-28, n=2,100, 2.15pp margin, 95% confidence, registration BR-01084/2026. THE WEEK HAS THREE FIRST-ROUND GAP READINGS AND THEY DO NOT AGREE: 9.1pp at AtlasIntel of Jul 29, 6pp at PoderData of Jul 30 and 9.3pp here. The outlier is PoderData, not Vox. RENAN SANTOS at 3.0% closes the sequence of THREE consecutive institutes cutting him: 7.8% at AtlasIntel, 4% at PoderData and 3.0% now. With the price at 8.15%, the distance between market and polling reaches 5.15pp, the widest in the window, against the 0.90pp the panel recorded on Jul 29. CAIADO at 5.5% has here his BEST national polling of the window, above PoderData's 5% and AtlasIntel's 3.1%, on the same day his price fell 0.80pp. The institute also reports that, between May and July, Lula gained 7.3pp and Flávio lost 2.7pp within its own series, reversing a lead that had belonged to the senator; the panel reproduces this as the institute's claim, because it is an internal comparison of theirs. This round did NOT publish approval or rejection.
polls.source: Vox Brasil via Metrópoles, Revista Fórum, Contracs Jul 31

polls.note: PoderData/Aya national poll published Jul 30 (Poder360, CNN Brasil, Metrópoles, Gazeta do Povo). First round Lula 41% x Flávio 35% (gap +6pp), with Caiado 5%, Renan Santos 4%, Zema 3% and Augusto Cury 3%, plus 5% blank or void and 4% who did not answer. Runoff Lula 46% x Flávio 43% (gap +3pp), a statistical tie by the 2pp margin. Field Jul 26-29, n=2,400, telephone on mobile and landline, 677 municipalities across the 27 states, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, registration BR-07845/2026. THE COMPARISON THAT COUNTS IS WITH THE HOUSE ITSELF, and there the first-round gap did NOT move: it was 6pp on Jul 16 (40% x 34%) and it is 6pp now (41% x 35%), with the top two each gaining 1pp, inside the margin. Against AtlasIntel of Jul 29, which gave 9.1pp, the difference is 3.1pp, but comparing different houses published a day apart and calling that a tightening is swapping rulers mid-measurement: it is a house effect, the same one the panel recorded on Jul 16, when PoderData contradicted Quaest with Lula IDENTICAL in both and the whole disagreement on Flávio. RENAN SANTOS FALLS from 6% to 4% inside the house itself, the round's largest individual swing, and that UNDOES the convergence the panel recorded on Jul 29 based on AtlasIntel's 7.8%: the distance between price (8.45%) and polling reopens from 0.90pp to 4.45pp. CAIADO rises from 4% to 5%. ZEMA falls from 4% to 3%. APPROVAL personal 43% x 49% disapproval (it was 46% x 47% in the institute's Jul 22 round, down 3pp and up 2pp) and GOVERNMENT rating 44% x 50%. MANAGEMENT 34% good or very good, 16% fair and 47% poor or terrible, with poor or terrible up 10pp against Jul 22, a big jump for two weeks. REJECTION: Lula 49% and Flávio 49%, TIED, when AtlasIntel of Jul 29 gave 49.4% x 52.9%. The institute also reported statistical ties in the runoff against Zema and against Caiado, but the panel does NOT record those numbers because it could not verify them in a primary source.
polls.source: PoderData/Aya via Poder360, CNN Brasil, Metrópoles, Gazeta do Povo Jul 30

polls.note: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel)/Bloomberg national poll released on Jul 29 (CNN Brasil, JOTA, Poder360, Metrópoles, Exame, Estadão, CartaCapital, VEJA, Brasil de Fato), the largest sample in the window with 5,021 interviews, ahead of the 5,000 of the institute's own Jul 1 round, and with the smallest margin in the window, 1pp, tied with that same Jul 1 round. It had declared publication to the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) for Jul 28 and came out a day later, which closes the absence the panel recorded yesterday. In the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): Lula 44.9%, Flávio Bolsonaro 35.8%, Renan Santos 7.8%, Ronaldo Caiado 3.1%, Romeu Zema 2.8%, Samara Martins 2.1%, Augusto Cury 1.6%, Cabo Daciolo 0.1%, Hertz Dias 0.1%, with 0.6% void or blank and 1% who do not know. In a scenario reduced to five names, Lula goes to 47.4% and Flávio to 37.0% (CNN Brasil). In the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), Lula wins the six scenarios he appears in: 49.2% x 42.9% against Flávio, 49.2% x 43.9% against Jair, 48.8% x 42.5% against Michelle, 48.6% x 39.6% against Zema, 48.2% x 38.9% against Caiado and 47.6% x 30.2% against Renan Santos. In the two scenarios without him, Haddad 44.3% x Flávio 43.7%, a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico), and Alckmin 45.8% x Flávio 42.7%. Rejection: Flávio 52.9%, Lula 49.4% and Jair 42.6%. Approval of Lula's performance 47.6% against 51.2% disapproval. Government rating: 37.9% great or good, 12.7% fair and 49.3% bad or terrible. Field Jul 22 to 27, n=5,021, 1pp margin, 95% confidence, protocol BR-08602/2026, cost of R$ 80,000, self-funded. READING: against the institute's own Jul 1 round (field Jun 25-30), BOTH front-runners fall, Lula from 46.3% to 44.9% and Flávio from 36.6% to 35.8%, and the first-round gap narrows from 9.7pp to 9.1pp. In the direct runoff, Lula goes from 48.8% to 49.2% and Flávio from 42.3% to 42.9%, with the gap moving from 6.5pp to 6.3pp. With a 1pp margin, all of those individual moves sit inside the noise, and the honest reading is stability, not advance or retreat. What moves outside the margin is the government rating: approval rises 1.7pp, from 45.9% to 47.6%, and disapproval falls 1.1pp, from 52.3% to 51.2%, keeping disapproval ahead by the same method. THREE FINDINGS FOR THE PANEL: first, Renan Santos at 7.8% is his second-highest national reading in the window, below the 9% from Real Time on Jul 21 and above the 6% from PoderData/Aya on Jul 16, the 5% from [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) on Jul 27 and the 3% from [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha), Gerp and Indexa, which means the dispersion between institutes remains open and now with the largest sample in the window sitting in the middle of it. Second, Caiado appears at 3.1%, half the 6% BTG/Nexus measured two days earlier, and in the runoff he loses 48.2% to 38.9%, well away from the statistical tie of 45% to 43% in that survey: the divergence over Caiado the panel recorded on Jul 27 between Nexus and Datafolha gains a third measurement, and it lands on Datafolha's side. Third, Lula wins the six runoffs he appears in and none of those margins fits inside the 1pp margin: the tightest is 5.3pp against JAIR Bolsonaro (49.2% to 43.9%), and not against Flávio, who sits at 6.3pp (49.2% to 42.9%). In other words, by the same survey, the father tests better than the son in the runoff, even if the difference between the two scenarios, 1.0pp, sits at the edge of the margin.
polls.source: AtlasIntel/Bloomberg via CNN Brasil, JOTA, Poder360, Metrópoles, Exame, Estadão, CartaCapital, VEJA and Brasil de Fato, Jul 29. TSE registration BR-08602/2026.

polls.note: National [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) poll released on Jul 27 (institute site nexus.fsb.com.br, Folha de S.Paulo, CNN Brasil, JOTA, CartaCapital, Poder360, VEJA, Estado de Minas, Metrópoles, Money Times), the first national survey whose fieldwork sits entirely AFTER the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention that formalized Flávio on Jul 25. In the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): Lula 42%, Flávio Bolsonaro 33%, Ronaldo Caiado 6%, Renan Santos 5%, Romeu Zema 3%. In the head-to-head [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), Lula 47% x Flávio 43%. The other scenarios: Lula 45% x Caiado 43%, Lula 46% x Zema 42% and Lula 47% x Renan Santos 39%. Rejection: Flávio 50%, Lula 48%. Government assessment: 36% excellent or good (15% excellent, 21% good), 20% fair and 43% poor or terrible (9% poor, 34% terrible). Lula's personal approval 47% x disapproval 49%, with 4% who did not answer, against 47% x 47% in the Jul 13 round. Decided vote rose to 73%, with 25% willing to change, reversing the fall from 74% to 70% recorded on Jul 13. Fieldwork Jul 24-26, n=2,004, telephone across all regions, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) filing BR-01489/2026, commissioned by Banco BTG Pactual. READING: against the institute's own Jul 13 round, Lula rises from 40% to 42% and Flávio falls from 34% to 33%, meaning the first-round gap widens from 6pp to 9pp, with both moves inside the margin. In the runoff the difference goes from 3pp to 4pp, also inside the margin, which is a nominal widening and a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) at the same time. THE FINDING IS ELSEWHERE, and it is Caiado: he ties Lula statistically at 45% to 43%, the narrowest of the four runoff scenarios in this poll, and he gains against the previous round. That INVERTS the [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) poll of Jul 24, published three days earlier, in which Lula beat Caiado 47% to 40%, seven points, the most comfortable margin in the panel. Two top-tier institutes, with fieldwork two days apart, reach opposite conclusions about which challenger is the most competitive. AFOS records the divergence and does not arbitrate which one is right. On Renan Santos, the poll measures him at 5% in the first round, above Datafolha's 3% and below Real Time's 9% on Jul 21, keeping the dispersion between institutes open.
polls.source: BTG/Nexus via the institute site (nexus.fsb.com.br), Folha de S.Paulo, CNN Brasil, JOTA, CartaCapital, Poder360, VEJA, Estado de Minas, Metrópoles and Money Times Jul 27. TSE filing BR-01489/2026.

polls.note: National [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) released on the evening of Jul 24 (G1, Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão, CNN Brasil, O Globo, CartaCapital), the first Tier 1 poll after party conventions began and after the new round of US tariffs. In the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): Lula 40%, Flávio Bolsonaro 32%, Caiado 4%, Zema 3%, Renan Santos 3%, Augusto Cury 2%, Samara Martins, Cabo Daciolo and Rui Costa Pimenta 1% each, Hertz Dias, Edmilson Costa and Leonardo Avalanche 0%; blank and null 8%, don't know 3%. In the head-to-head [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), Lula 48% x Flávio 43%. Lula wins the other scenarios tested: 47% x Caiado 40% and 48% x Zema 40%. Rejection: Flávio 48%, Lula 46%, Zema 13%, Caiado 12%, Cabo Daciolo 12%, Renan Santos 12%. Fieldwork Jul 22-24, n=2,004, face-to-face, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) filing BR-01166/2026. READING: this is STABILITY, not a reversal. Against the previous Datafolha (Jun 20, fieldwork Jun 17-19, same n and same margin), Lula goes from 41% to 40% and Flávio from 31% to 32% in the first round, while in the runoff Lula goes from 47% to 48% and Flávio stays at 43%. The two readings moved in OPPOSITE directions and both inside the margin, which is the signature of sampling noise and not of a trend. Rejection came in identical to June for both names (48% and 46%). IT SETTLES THE RENAN CASE: with Renan at 3%, Datafolha joins Gerp Jul 22 and Indexa Jul 21, meaning three of the four most recent national polls measure him at 3%, and the 9% from Real Time Jul 21 is left isolated. It is the heaviest polling reading in the set and the one that most tightens the distortion against his market price.
polls.source: Datafolha via G1, Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão, CNN Brasil, O Globo, CartaCapital Jul 24. TSE filing BR-01166/2026.

polls.note: Gerp/AESP national poll published July 22 (Exame, Gazeta do Povo, CNN Brasil, Poder360, CartaCapital, Jovem Pan, Revista Oeste). Tie in R1: Lula 38% x Flávio 38%; Zema, Renan Santos and Caiado at 3% each; Augusto Cury, Joaquim Barbosa, Cabo Daciolo and Samara Martins 1%; none of them 5%, don't know 7%. In R2, Flávio 46% x Lula 45% (Flávio numerically ahead, [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) within the 2.19pp margin). Lula wins the remaining scenarios: 44% x Caiado 41%, 44% x Zema 38%, 45% x Renan 35%. Rejection: Lula 47%, Flávio 46%. Fieldwork July 15-17, n=2,000, telephone, margin 2.19pp, 95% confidence, commissioned by AESP, protocol BR-05026/2026. CONTEXT: Gerp keeps the pro-Flávio OUTLIER pattern already recorded on June 24 and July 8, consistently more favorable to Flávio than the Tier 1 consensus ([Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) July 15 gave Lula +12pp in R1 and +8pp in R2; [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) comes on July 24). Smaller institute, reliability 3. IT SETTLES THE RENAN CASE: with Renan at 3%, Gerp lines up with Indexa (3%) against Real Time (9%), meaning two of the three most recent national polls measure him at 3%. [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket), which on the SAME day raised Renan's price to 10.70%, became even more isolated, and it is Real Time's 9% that starts to look like the outlier among the polls, rather than the market being right. Real Time's second signal was not confirmed either: Gerp puts Lula ahead of Caiado in R2 (44x41), not the tie Real Time had indicated.
polls.source: Gerp/AESP via Exame, Gazeta do Povo, CNN Brasil, Poder360, CartaCapital, Jovem Pan, Revista Oeste 22/Jul. Registro TSE BR-05026/2026.

polls.note: Indexa Pesquisas national poll published July 21 (JOTA, CartaCapital, Gazeta do Povo, Diário do Grande ABC, UOL, Money Times, Poder360), one of the TWO national polls released on the same day, breaking five days without new voting intention. R1 Lula 41% x Flávio 30% (gap +11pp), with Caiado 6%, Zema 3%, Renan Santos 3%, Augusto Cury and Joaquim Barbosa 1%. R2 Lula 46% x Flávio 39% (gap +7pp), and Lula also beats Zema, Caiado and Renan in the runoff. Approval 49% x disapproval 48%, a tie within the margin, the least negative reading of the sample. Rejection: Flávio 50%, Lula 49%, [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico). 51% say Lula does not deserve another four years. On the tariff crisis with the United States, 30% blame Flávio and 28% Lula. Fieldwork July 16-19, n=2,000, telephone, margin 2.2pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-02904/2026. READING: it is the same house that on June 23 gave R1 42x31 and R2 47x40, now with slight narrowing within its own yardstick (R1 +11pp, R2 +7pp). It diverges from Real Time of the same day precisely in the runoff: Indexa gives Lula +7, Real Time gives a statistical tie of +3. The two agree on the first round (Lula 40-41, Flávio 30-33).
polls.source: Indexa Pesquisas via JOTA, CartaCapital, Gazeta do Povo, Diário do Grande ABC, UOL, Money Times, Poder360 21/Jul. Registro TSE BR-02904/2026.

polls.note: Real Time Big Data national poll published July 21 (Exame, CNN Brasil, Brasil 247, CartaCapital, Gazeta do Povo, Poder360, InfoMoney, VEJA, GZH), the second of the two national polls of the day. R1 Lula 40% x Flávio 33% (gap +7pp), with Renan Santos at 9% and Caiado at 7%. R2 Lula 45% x Flávio 42% (gap +3pp, [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico)); Lula 43% x Caiado 44% (Caiado numerically ahead, statistical tie within the margin); Lula 44% x Renan 35%. Approval 46% x disapproval 50%. Rejection: Flávio 50%, Lula 48%. Fieldwork July 18-20, n=2,000, telephone, margin 2pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-09247/2026. TWO FINDINGS: (1) Renan Santos rises to 9% in the first round, his highest mark in a national poll in the 30-day window (the previous ceiling was 6% at PoderData July 16) and practically the level [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) was already giving him (8.85%). The market x polling distortion that had been the most glaring case on the panel was validated by THIS house, but Indexa of the SAME day measures him at 3%, six points away, so it is dispersion among institutes, not convergence. (2) Caiado appears numerically ahead of Lula in a head-to-head runoff (44% x 43%), and VEJA records that Lula's most competitive opponent in the runoff is not Flávio. The two readings of today agree on the first round (Lula 40-41, Flávio 30-33) and diverge on the second (Indexa Lula +7, Real Time a tie).
polls.source: Real Time Big Data via Exame, CNN Brasil, Brasil 247, CartaCapital, Gazeta do Povo, Poder360, InfoMoney, VEJA, GZH 21/Jul. Registro TSE BR-09247/2026.

polls.note: PoderData/Aya national poll published July 16 (Poder360, CNN Brasil, Gazeta do Povo, CartaCapital, ND Mais). R1 Lula 40% x Flávio 34% (gap +6pp), with Renan Santos 6%, Caiado 4%, Zema 4%, Augusto Cury 3%. R2 Lula 45% x Flávio 43% (gap +2pp), a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) by the 2pp margin. Fieldwork July 12-15, n=2,400, telephone (mobile and landline), 685 municipalities across the 27 states, margin 2pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-00059/2026. IT CONTRADICTS YESTERDAY'S QUAEST: 24 hours after Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) gave R1 +12pp and R2 +8pp, PoderData returns the runoff to a statistical tie. Lula is IDENTICAL in both (40% in R1, 45% in R2). The entire disagreement is about Flávio: 28% against 34% in R1, 37% against 43% in R2, six points apart between the two best readings of the week. HOUSE EFFECT, not a turn: in PoderData's own series, Flávio goes from 36% (June 25) to 34%, that is, he also FALLS, only from a higher level. The two houses agree on direction (Flávio retreating) and disagree on level. Comparing yesterday's Quaest with today's PoderData and calling the difference a movement means switching yardsticks mid-measurement. RENAN SANTOS at 6%, his highest mark among the national polls in the 30-day window (the ceiling was 4% before), and a rise within the house itself (4% on June 25). APPROVAL diverges sharply: 42% approve x 51% disapprove, against 48% x 47% from yesterday's Quaest, nine points of difference in disapproval. REJECTION: Lula and Flávio tied at 48%, against Flávio's 57% at Quaest.
polls.source: PoderData/Aya via Poder360, CNN Brasil, Gazeta do Povo, CartaCapital, ND Mais 16/Jul

polls.note: Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) national poll published July 15 (G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, GZH, VEJA, JOTA, Brasil de Fato, Metrópoles, Gazeta do Povo, Revista Oeste), the HIGHEST reliability of the week. It BREAKS the narrowing sequence of the previous three: R1 Lula 40% x Flávio 28% (gap +12pp), with Caiado 4%, Renan Santos 3%, Zema 2%. R2 Lula 45% x Flávio 37% (gap +8pp), Lula's largest runoff advantage among the July national polls. Lula moves up and Flávio down in both rounds, and Quaest points for the first time to a chance of Lula winning in the first round (VEJA, SRzd). Fieldwork July 10-13, n=2,004, in person, margin 2pp, 95% confidence, registered with the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse). CRITICAL READING: it comes after Gerp July 8 (Flávio ahead in R2), BTG/[Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) July 13 (47x44, statistical tie) and Futura/Apex July 14 (46.3x46.1, a tie), which together suggested narrowing. Quaest, the institute with the highest reliability in the sample, goes in the OPPOSITE direction and reopens the lead. The runoff range for the week now runs from a tie (Futura/Apex) to Lula +8 (Quaest). DIVERGENCE WITH THE MARKET: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) gives Lula 61.50% x Flávio 25.30% (gap +36.20pp). The level gap remains wide, though below the cycle peak (+39.5pp on July 3), but the market's direction (Lula ahead) gained the backing of the best poll, and the market corrected Renan Santos downward (8.50%, down 1.65pp) toward what polling declares.
polls.source: Genial/Quaest via G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, GZH, VEJA, JOTA, Brasil de Fato, Metrópoles, Gazeta do Povo, Revista Oeste 15/Jul

polls.note: Futura/Apex (Futura Inteligência) national poll published July 14 (Gazeta do Povo, Exame, Metrópoles, Revista Fórum, Brasil 247). SECOND of the week's national polls and the THIRD in a row to indicate narrowing. Prompted R1: Lula 40.1% x Flávio 36.8%, a difference of 3.3pp against a margin of 2.2pp, meaning the intervals overlap. Caiado 5.0%, Zema 3.7%, Renan Santos 2.6%. R2: Lula 46.3% x Flávio 46.1%, a difference of 0.2 point, the TIGHTEST TIE recorded in this cycle. Fieldwork July 7-11, n=2,000, telephone, universe of Brazilian voters aged 16 or over, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) protocol BR-07294/2026, margin 2.2pp, 95% confidence. CRITICAL READING: Gerp of July 8 (a small-institute outlier) signaled the narrowing, BTG/[Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) of July 13 confirmed it coming from the top tier, and Futura/Apex of July 14 takes the runoff to an almost perfect tie. It is no longer an isolated institute. The runoff range today: Gerp 42x45 (Flávio ahead), Futura/Apex 46.3x46.1 (tie), BTG/Nexus 47x44 ([statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico)), Meio/Ideia 45x40, AtlasIntel 48.8x42.3. DIVERGENCE WITH THE MARKET: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) gives Lula 60.50% x Flávio 24.85%, a gap of +35.65pp, and DID NOT MOVE with any of the three polls. It is the sharpest level divergence of the cycle.
polls.source: Futura/Apex (Futura Inteligência) via Gazeta do Povo, Exame, Metrópoles, Revista Fórum, Brasil 247, 14/Jul. Registro TSE BR-07294/2026.

polls.note: BTG/[Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) national poll published July 13 (the institute's own site, Folha, Poder360, VEJA, CartaCapital, Gazeta do Povo). FIRST of the week's four national polls. R1: Lula 40% (down 2pp from the 42% of June 29), Flávio 34% (flat), Caiado 5%, Renan Santos 4%, Zema 4%. R2: Lula 47% x Flávio 44%, a difference of 3pp, a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) within the 2pp margin, exactly the same as the previous round of June 29. Fieldwork July 10-12, n=2,003, telephone in all regions, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) protocol BR-07981/2026. CRITICAL READING: it confirms the narrowing that Gerp of July 8 signaled, and now coming from a top-tier institute, not an outlier. The runoff picture becomes dispersed: Gerp 42x45 (Flávio ahead), BTG/Nexus 47x44 (statistical tie), Meio/Ideia 45x40, AtlasIntel 48.8x42.3. A little-cited and relevant data point: decided vote fell from 74% to 70%, meaning more voters willing to change with less than 90 days to the first round. DIVERGENCE WITH THE MARKET: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) gives Lula 60.50% x Flávio 23.85% (gap +36.65pp) while this poll has the runoff at +3pp and within the margin.
polls.source: BTG/Nexus via site do instituto (nexus.fsb.com.br), Folha de S.Paulo, Poder360, VEJA, CartaCapital, Gazeta do Povo 13/Jul

polls.note: Meio/Ideia (Instituto Ideia with Canal Meio) national poll published July 8 (JOTA, Estadão, CartaCapital, Correio Braziliense, Brasil de Fato, Poder360, Revista Fórum), the first national poll with new numbers since [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) July 1. Lula leads every scenario: R1 Lula 40.4% x Flávio 32% (gap +8.4pp), with Caiado 4%, Zema 2.5%, Aécio Neves and Renan Santos 2%, Augusto Cury 1.5%, Joaquim Barbosa and Cabo Daciolo 0.5%. R2 Lula 45% x Flávio 40% (gap +5pp, blank/null 10.5%, undecided 4.5%); R2 Lula 45% x Michelle 36%. The institute's founder noted that Lula's re-election remains in a fragile position despite the lead (UOL). Fieldwork July 3-6, n=1,500, margin 2.5pp, 95% confidence. [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) protocol BR-05628/2026. It moved in the same direction as the market (Lula ahead), but with a tighter runoff (+5pp) than the lead of real money (+39pp).
polls.source: Meio/Ideia via JOTA, Estadão, CartaCapital, Correio Braziliense, Brasil de Fato, Poder360, Revista Fórum 08/Jul

polls.note: Gerp/AESP national poll published July 8 (Poder360, Gazeta do Povo, Exame, CNN Brasil, CartaCapital). Tie in R1: Lula 36% x Flávio 36%; Caiado 4%, Renan Santos and Zema 2%, Cury and Joaquim Barbosa 1%; don't know 11%, none of them 6%. In R2, Flávio 45% x Lula 42% (Flávio ahead, but within the 2.2pp margin). Lula wins the remaining R2 scenarios (Michelle 45x41, Caiado 40x36, Zema 41x36, Damares 41x34, Pontes 42x34, Marinho 41x32, Renan 41x30). Fieldwork July 3-7, n=2,000, margin 2.2pp, 95% confidence, commissioned by AESP (the São Paulo association of radio and television companies), cost R$ 34,899. [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) protocol BR-03067/2026. CRITICAL CONTEXT: published on the SAME DAY as Meio/Ideia (BR-05628/2026), with the OPPOSITE winner in the runoff (Ideia gives Lula 45x40; Gerp gives Flávio 45x42). Gerp keeps the OUTLIER pattern already recorded in the June 24 round: it is consistently more favorable to Flávio than the Tier 1 consensus ([Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha), Indexa, BTG/[Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg), CNT/MDA), all with Lula comfortable. Smaller institute, reliability 3. MAXIMUM DIVERGENCE WITH THE MARKET: while Gerp has a tie in R1 and Flávio winning R2, [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) prices Lula 60.5% x Flávio 23.25% (gap 37.25pp on July 12). It is one of the largest market x polling disconnects of the cycle so far. Entry added on July 12 after a scope audit: the registration came from the TSE with no methodology text (scope_source=none), was classified as unknown and fell outside the national cut; NATIONAL scope confirmed by 2 independent primary sources (Poder360 + Gazeta do Povo).
polls.source: Gerp/AESP via Poder360, Gazeta do Povo, Exame, CNN Brasil, CartaCapital 08/Jul

approvalData.note: Genial/Quaest from Aug 5: 48% approve, 47% disapprove, a positive net of 1pp, with performance at 36% positive, 26% fair and 36% negative. Meio/Ideia from the same window: 48.5% approve and 49% disapprove (Estadão, Aug 5), a negative net. BTG/Nexus from Aug 3: 47% x 48%. All three sit within any margin of one another, and that is why the sign of the net depends on the house, not on the electorate.
approvalData.source: Genial/Quaest Aug 5, 2026 (fieldwork Jul 31 to Aug 3, n=2,004, in person, 120 municipalities, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, commissioned by Banco Genial, BR-06591/2026), released by G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, Valor Econômico, O Globo, Estadão, Money Times and Poder360. Within-house comparison against the Genial/Quaest round of Jul 15 (fieldwork Jul 10 to Jul 13, n=2,004, BR-07181/2026), via Poder360. The BTG/Nexus reading of Aug 3 (BR-02874/2026) is kept in the text as the second house.

polymarketComparison.note: THE PRICES IN THIS SECTION ARE FROM THE READING OF AUG 6, 19:44 UTC. AFOS only publishes a price that two independent readings confirm, and the presidential market returned the same values in three readings across twenty minutes. One exception is declared: in the third-place contract for the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), Renan Santos slipped from 57.50% to 56.50% in the same window, so it appears as a range and not as a firm number. THE BALLOT SIDE IS NOT FROM TODAY: there is no new national poll since Aug 5, when Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) and Meio/Ideia came out. The four national polls in the field close between Aug 9 and Aug 10.
polymarketComparison.sources: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) prices via the AFOS proxy, locked capture at 19:11 UTC on Aug 3 (scripts/capture-guard.ts). There is no confirmed market reading on Aug 4 and Aug 5. Polls: Genial/Quaest BR-06591/2026 and Meio/Ideia BR-04579/2026, both from Aug 5, fieldwork Jul 31 to Aug 3, released by G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, Valor Econômico, O Globo, Estadão, Exame, Gazeta do Povo and JOTA. TSE sweep on Aug 5: 537 registrations, none newly inserted.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.tendenciaPesquisa: TWO FRESH NATIONAL POLLS TODAY, both with him ahead in every scenario. [Genial/Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) (n=2,004, fieldwork Jul 31 to Aug 3, in person, 2pp margin, BR-06591/2026): 39% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and 44% x 39% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) against Flávio, also beating Zema 46% x 34%, Caiado 45% x 37% and Renan Santos 45% x 35%. Meio/Ideia (n=1,500, telephone, 2.5pp margin, BR-04579/2026): 43% in the first round and 48.5% x 43% in the runoff, winning all four scenarios. WITHIN THE HOUSE, which is the valid comparison: at Quaest he gives up 1pp in the first round, from 40% to 39%, and 1pp in the runoff, from 45% to 44%, both inside the 2pp margin; at Ideia he RISES, from 40.4% to 43%. The two houses give him movements of opposite sign in the same fieldwork window, which is information about method and not about the electorate. APPROVAL at 48% against 47% at Quaest, a number identical to its own Jul 15 round, with administration ratings repeating 36% positive, 26% average and 36% negative.
candidates.tendenciaPolymarket: [Aug 6 reading, 19:44 UTC] At 64.50% (vol USD 8.09M cumulative). Down 1.00pp against the Aug 3 reading. The gap over Flávio went from +40.05pp to +37.75pp, a fifth day running of narrowing since the +41.80pp peak of Aug 1. In the 88-day series his peak is 66.50%, from Aug 1.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.tendenciaPesquisa: TODAY'S TWO NATIONAL POLLS put him up within his own house. At [Genial/Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) he goes from 28% to 30% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and from 37% to 39% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), a 2pp gain in each, which sits at the edge of the 2pp margin and therefore cannot be separated from noise with confidence. At Meio/Ideia he goes from 32% to 35% in the first round and from 40% to 43% in the runoff, a 3pp gain, above the 2.5pp margin. The gap against Lula lands at 9pp at Quaest and 8pp at Ideia, against the 4pp that [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) measured on Aug 3: the 4pp level still belongs to one house alone, and what today's two rounds confirm is DIRECTION, not level. REJECTION in the Quaest round: 54% say they would not vote for him and 41% would. Lula has 52% rejection and 45% voting intention. Among the TOP TWO CANDIDATES in this round, the only ones whose rejection figures were released, his is the higher. The round did not publish rejection for the other names, so the panel does not extend the comparison to the rest of the field.
candidates.tendenciaPolymarket: [Aug 6 reading, 19:44 UTC] At 26.75% (vol USD 8.05M cumulative). Up 1.30pp against the Aug 3 reading, back to that day’s level. It is not an extreme: 34 of the 88 days in the series matched or beat it, with a peak of 43.30% on May 9 and a floor of 22.00% on Jul 3. In the second-place contract he sits at 87.50%, against 80.50% on Aug 3.

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.tendenciaPesquisa: Today's two national polls measure him in the same narrow band: 4% at [Genial/Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest), against 3% in its own Jul 15 round, and 4.7% at Meio/Ideia, against 2% in its own Jul 8 round. In the runoffs he is the worst placed of both rounds: he loses to Lula 45% x 35% at Quaest and 48% x 34.7% at Ideia. With that, six consecutive national polls measure him between 3% and 4.7%, after the 7.8% from [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) on Jul 29, and the isolated high reading remains the exception of the set. He declared on Wednesday that, if elected, he will not comply with single-justice [STF](/en/glossary#stf) rulings and that he will deal with the Centrão.
candidates.tendenciaPolymarket: [Aug 6 reading, 19:44 UTC] At 6.85% (vol USD 9.10M cumulative). Down 0.60pp against the Aug 3 reading. In the third-place contract for the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) AFOS publishes a RANGE and not a firm number: his price ran from 57.50% to 56.50% inside the same window, and only what two independent readings confirm goes out as a price.

candidates.name: Ronaldo Caiado
candidates.tendenciaPesquisa: [Genial/Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) gives 4% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), the same as its own Jul 15 round, and Meio/Ideia gives 5.7%, against 4% in its own Jul 8 round. In the runoffs he loses to Lula 45% x 37% at Quaest and 48.5% x 40% at Ideia. The disagreement between houses about him remains open inside the same fieldwork window: 4% at one house and 5.7% at the other, with both fielding from Jul 31 to Aug 3. He mocked Lula and Flávio on Wednesday, saying both are more worried about saving the family than the country.
candidates.tendenciaPolymarket: [Aug 6 reading, 19:44 UTC] At 1.85% (vol USD 5.56M cumulative). Up 0.70pp against the Aug 3 reading. In the third-place contract for the first round he went from 25.00% to 32.50%, a rise of 7.50pp.

candidates.name: Tarcísio
candidates.tendenciaPesquisa: Neither [Genial/Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) nor Meio/Ideia tests him in any presidential scenario, first round or runoff. Absence of testing in two national polls on the same day is information the panel records, instead of repeating old data as if it were new. He is running for RE-ELECTION as governor of São Paulo, made official by [Republicanos](/en/glossary#republicanos) on Aug 1.
candidates.tendenciaPolymarket: [Aug 6 reading, 19:44 UTC] At 0.05% (vol USD 13.87M cumulative), unchanged against the Aug 3 reading. It remains the legacy anomaly of the presidential book: the largest cumulative volume of all and the lowest price among the names cited. Volume measures traded history, not present conviction.

candidates.name: Romeu Zema
candidates.tendenciaPesquisa: [Genial/Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) gives 2% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), the same as its own Jul 15 round, and Meio/Ideia gives 2.6%, against 2.5% in its own Jul 8 round. In the runoffs he is the opponent Lula beats by the widest margin at Quaest, 46% x 34%, and he loses 48.5% x 37% at Ideia. In the polling he is flat at both houses. He closed his ticket on Aug 4 with senator Eduardo Girão, of [Novo](/en/glossary#novo), and was the first of the third-way names to settle the running mate.
candidates.tendenciaPolymarket: [Aug 6 reading, 19:44 UTC] At 0.45% (vol USD 4.82M cumulative). Up 0.20pp against the Aug 3 reading, which at this level carries almost no informational value. A series caveat that still holds: his maximum is 10.10%, from Apr 26.

candidates.name: Fernando Haddad
candidates.tendenciaPesquisa: Neither [Genial/Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) nor Meio/Ideia tests him in any scenario, first round or runoff, so he still has no polling. The caveat stands and needs to be said plainly: he is NOT a presidential candidate, he is running for governor of São Paulo, and any scenario including him is a poll hypothesis, not a candidacy under way.
candidates.tendenciaPolymarket: [Aug 6 reading, 19:44 UTC] At 0.15% (vol USD 6.74M cumulative), unchanged against the Aug 3 reading. He is not a candidate, so the contract prices a replacement scenario on the PT ticket and not a race under way.
